purpose: Thresholds for the Today view's daily field conditions (TODAY_ECONOMICS_FOOTPRINT_SPEC.md section 10.1 item 4): IMD daily rainfall classes, crop standing-water practice windows and crop heat-stress thresholds; since 2026-11-03 (WEATHER_DEPTH_SPEC.md section 6, packet B) also the soil-moisture classes, the wetness thresholds and the gust threshold. Read by apps/api/src/services/today/conditions.ts.

conventions.units: Rain in mm per 24 hours (IMD 0830 to 0830 IST day); temperatures in degrees C (daily maximum).
conventions.nulls: A missing value means no cited figure was found or the crop was not searched in this pass; it never means zero.
conventions.rainBands: Each class applies from its lowerMm (inclusive) up to the next class's lowerMm; 0 mm is 'none' (IMD prints DRY separately).

rainClasses.locator: Map legend (Agartala); 'Rainfall amount (mm)' line printed under each warning table (national bulletin)
rainClasses.note: The Agartala legend prints very heavy as 115.5 - 204.4 mm, overlapping the heavy band's upper edge 115.5; the IMD national bulletin prints very heavy as 115.6 - 204.4 and extremely heavy as 204.5 or more, which is used here. The legend prints very light as 0.0 - 2.4 with DRY as its own class, so very light starts above 0 mm.

waterPractice.locator: Water Management for Different Ecosystem: Transplanted lowland rice; Wet Seeded Puddled Lowland Rice; Water stress: Maturity stage
waterPractice.note: Transplanted lowland rice: 2 cm for seven days after transplanting, then cyclic 5 cm submergence throughout the crop period; drained about 7 to 10 days before harvest. Wet-seeded rice is only wetted with a thin film in the first week, so standing water is taken from day 7 for methods other than transplanting. Dry-seeded and semi-dry rice are irrigated to shallow depths later; they are not modelled separately. Tamil Nadu (TNAU) practice, used for every state until a state-specific page is cited.

heatThresholds.locator: Mechanisms: High Temperature At Flowering, paragraph 2
heatThresholds.note: Secondary source: a NSW Agriculture and Rice CRC travel report citing Yoshida (1981), Fundamentals of Rice Crop Science, IRRI; the original was not retrieved. The threshold is for the day of flowering; spikelet sterility also depends on duration, humidity and variety.

soilMoistureClasses.locator: Chapter 7, Evaporation component: Table 19 (Typical soil water characteristics for different soil types); 'Stage 1: energy limiting stage' and 'Stage 2: falling rate stage'
soilMoistureClasses.note: Table 19 gives, per USDA texture class, ranges of field capacity (fc), wilting point (wp) and readily evaporable water (REW, the depth evaporated from the topsoil in stage 1, while the surface stays wet). FAO 56 says that once stage 1 ends 'the soil surface is visibly dry'. The engine compares the grid cell's modelled 0 to 7 cm soil moisture (m3/m3) with the end of stage 1 over the evaporation layer: wet end = fcHigh - rewLowMm / (1000 x evaporationLayerM), dry end = fcLow - rewHighMm / (1000 x evaporationLayerM). At or above the wet end the topsoil is moist for any soil of that texture in the table's ranges; below the dry end it is past stage 1 (dry surface) for any of them; in between the table cannot tell and the rain rule decides. evaporationLayerM 0.10 is the layer depth Table 19 uses for its TEW column (FAO recommends 0.10 to 0.15 m where unknown); the model layer is 0 to 7 cm. The model's own soil texture and hydraulic parameters are not this field's; this is an uncalibrated comparison. The HTML prints silty clay field capacity as '0-30 - 0.42'; read as 0.30 to 0.42. Wilting points are kept for reference; the rule does not use them.

wetnessThresholds.note: No Indian agromet (IMD GKMS district bulletins from TNAU and KAU, searched 2026-11-03) or FAO document found in this pass states a crop-independent daily leaf-wetness or humidity figure for fungal spread: the bulletins say high humidity, dew or high morning humidity without rain favour disease, and give numbers only for named diseases. Hourly RH of 90% or more is a common leaf-wetness proxy in the literature (Hamada et al. 2008, Brazil), but the pipeline stores daily means only. The thresholds are therefore engine assumptions (conditions.ts CONDITION_ASSUMPTIONS.wetness) and pressure.basis is engine_assumption. A later pass can put sourced {high, moderate} figures here with a sourceId; the engine then uses them and marks the basis sourced_threshold.

lodgingGust.note: No crop-independent gust threshold for lodging was found: IMD and OUAT/KAU agromet bulletins and IMD cyclone bulletins advise propping or bund care when strong wind is forecast and list lodging as an impact without a figure; laboratory critical wind speeds are cultivar-specific (maize stalk-breaking studies). The engine reuses the project's 60 km/h gust alert threshold (alerts.ts WEATHER_THRESHOLDS.windGustKmh), flagged as an alert threshold, not a lodging figure (CONDITION_ASSUMPTIONS.lodgingGust).

TNAU-AGRITECH-PADDY-WATER.title: Rice: Cultivation Practices >> Water Management
TNAU-AGRITECH-PADDY-WATER.publisher: TNAU Agritech Portal, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University
TNAU-AGRITECH-PADDY-WATER.locator: Transplanted lowland rice; Wet Seeded Puddled Lowland Rice; Maturity stage
TNAU-AGRITECH-PADDY-WATER.excerpt: Maintain 2 cm of water up to seven days of transplanting. After the establishment stage, cyclic submergence of water is the best practice for rice crop. This cyclic 5 cm submergence has to be continued throughout the crop period. ... During first one week just wet the soil by thin film of water. ... After yellowish ripening stage, there is no necessity for standing water. Water may be drained from the field about 7-10 days before harvest to facilitate harvesting.

CSU-RICE2001-HIGH-TEMP-FLOWERING.excerpt: Anthesis usually occurs between 1000 hours and 1200 hours, with temperature rising in the morning and exceeding the critical temperature (35oC) by 1000 hours in high temperature areas.
